note: Wednesday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Tue 28 Jul US close — the day before the FOMC decision (Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET). The dominant shift: risk assets de-risked into the Fed even as the tape ground to records. Metals gave back Monday's bounce (silver -2% to ~$57.5, gold -1.25% to ~$4,030) on a firmer dollar; oil kept sliding (Brent -4.8% to ~$84) as the Iran pause held and Iran opened Hormuz talks with Saudi/Oman; a global chip rout (NVDA $250B OpenAI-backstop worry) triggered a KOSPI circuit-breaker (~-10%) and Nikkei -4.4%. S&P +0.21% to a record 7,428.78 and Dow +1.03% on falling oil/strong earnings; Nasdaq -0.22%. Crypto fell (BTC -2.5%, ETH -3.2%). 8 of 12 items are dated Tue 28 Jul (last 24h). Every item source-verified.

items.headline: FOMC decides Wed 29 Jul: hawkish-hold base case, hike odds ~1-in-3 as oil eases
items.summary: The Fed (chaired by Kevin Warsh since May 2026) is expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, with the decision Wed 29 Jul 2pm ET and no SEP. Market pricing is ~64-66% hold vs ~34-36% for a 25bp hike; September hike odds still sit near 80% after the earlier oil/inflation spike repriced tightening hard. Warsh has been hawkish in rhetoric with no firm guidance. Q2 GDP and PCE also land this week.
items.actionable: A live ~1-in-3 hike is the core near-term threat to levered silver and SGX REITs, and the pre-FOMC de-risk already knocked silver back ~2% — keep the big USD cash pile (~3.5-3.75%) as productive dry powder and let the 29 Jul print resolve before redeploying into rate-sensitive names. A dovish Warsh surprise is the upside catalyst; a hawkish hold or hike the downside.

items.headline: Silver drops ~2% to ~$57.5, gold to ~$4,030 ahead of the Fed — Monday's bounce reverses
items.summary: Silver fell ~2% to ~$57.5/oz and gold slipped ~1.25% to ~$4,030 on Tuesday on a firmer US dollar and pre-FOMC caution, reversing Monday's rebound (silver had hit ~$59.4, gold ~$4,098). GDX sat near $75.4 (YTD ~-12%). The Iran de-escalation that eased oil also removed a geopolitical bid under bullion, and silver — 2-3x more rate-sensitive than gold — gave back most.
items.actionable: The levered silver core is the portfolio's biggest short-term swing factor and it whipsawed straight back down once the pre-FOMC dollar bid took over — a reminder to hedge the silver-vs-gold spread into the 29 Jul print rather than chasing Monday's bounce with added leverage. Structural deficit thesis intact (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 avg); treat the FOMC as the next binary.

items.headline: US-Iran fighting pause holds; oil slides further — Brent ~$84, WTI ~$79; Iran in Hormuz talks
items.summary: The pause in US-Iran hostilities held into a further session Tuesday, with Iran holding Strait-of-Hormuz talks with Saudi Arabia and Oman. Brent fell ~4.8% to ~$84 and WTI ~4% to ~$79, extending Monday's collapse and further deflating the war/inflation premium. Tehran denied agreeing to a formal 10-day ceasefire, so the truce stays two-way, and the Houthi/Red Sea front remains a residual risk.
items.actionable: The extended oil slide keeps unwinding the inflation/rate-hike fear that pressures the rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) — but it also strips out the geopolitical bid that had supported metals, hence Tuesday's silver/gold pullback. Net: a dovish nudge to the Fed path at the cost of the small energy long; keep gold-heavy GDX as the hedge against the pause breaking down.

items.headline: Global chip rout: NVDA ~$250B OpenAI-backstop report sparks circular-financing fear; KOSPI circuit-breaker, Nikkei -4.4%
items.summary: A report that Nvidia is exploring up to ~$250B of AI-financing guarantees (plus a ~$350B OpenAI-linked chip deal) stoked AI-overcapacity/circular-financing fears, sending NVDA ~5% lower and cascading through Asia: South Korea's KOSPI hit a ~10% circuit-breaker and Japan's Nikkei fell 4.4% on Tuesday, with AI-name CDS at records. In Hong Kong semis sold off (Kingboard -10%+, SMIC gave up gains). China memory-maker CXMT surged 466% on its Shanghai debut, adding competition worry.
items.actionable: A deepening, portfolio-specific headwind for the chip leg of the HK-tech core (SMIC) — the sharp intra-sector divergence (Tencent/Alibaba/Xiaomi up, chips down) again argues for favoring the internet/consumer names over pure-semi exposure. Watch whether the AI-capex-peak narrative deepens through MSFT/META (Wed) and AAPL/AMZN (Thu) earnings; it is the main risk against the supportive China-stimulus backdrop.

items.headline: HK internet giants firm despite the chip rout: Hang Seng up a 4th straight session
items.summary: The Hang Seng rose ~0.4% for a fourth straight day and HS Tech +0.61% as Tencent, Alibaba and Xiaomi pushed higher and anchored the index even as semis (SMIC) retreated on the overnight US chip rout. The internet/platform sleeve is decoupling from the memory/AI-hardware weakness, helped by China's H2-stimulus signal and a record 3rd-largest weekly China equity inflow (+$21.3bn).
items.actionable: The HK-tech core's internet names (Tencent, Xiaomi) are proving resilient and are the preferred exposure over the SMIC chip leg while the semis rout runs — reinforced by the record weekly China inflow. Favor the platform names into Tencent's 12 Aug results; keep SMIC exposure lighter given the AI-capex/memory drag.

items.headline: S&P and Dow eke out record closes on oil retreat and strong earnings; Nasdaq dips on chip rotation
items.summary: US stocks ground higher on rotation: the S&P 500 added 0.21% to a record 7,428.78, the Dow gained 1.03% (to 52,747) on falling oil and strong earnings (Coca-Cola's best day since 2009), while the Nasdaq slipped 0.22% to 24,876.91 as the AI/semis rout capped gains. VIX eased to ~18.2. The tape reads mildly risk-on but semis-cautious into the Fed and the mega-cap earnings gauntlet.
items.actionable: The oil-down/rotation tape helped the cyclical and rate-sensitive names the book cares about (Dow, financials, and by extension S-REITs/metals on a softer inflation path) while the AI-capex unwind stays a headwind for the SMIC chip leg. Watch MSFT/META (Wed) and AAPL/AMZN (Thu) — a soft AI-capex readout would deepen the semis rotation into Asia.

items.headline: Crypto slides into the Fed: Bitcoin ~$63.5k (-2.5%), Ether ~$1,885 (-3.2%)
items.summary: After Monday's de-escalation-driven pop (ETH +4.4%), crypto de-risked ahead of the 29 Jul FOMC: Bitcoin opened around $63,300-63,700 (-2.5% vs Monday), Ether ~$1,878-1,891 (-3.2%) and Solana ~$73 (-4.1%). The crypto Fear & Greed reading slid to ~28 (Fear). The market continues to trade as a pure risk-appetite barometer off the macro rate channel rather than any crypto-specific catalyst.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto moves in lockstep with the silver/REIT rate-sensitivity trade — the same pre-FOMC de-risk that knocked silver down knocked crypto down, hence Ether's underperformance. Treat it as a barometer of the risk-relief impulse; a dovish Warsh would lift both crypto and the metals core, a hawkish print would pressure both.

items.headline: China Politburo delivers firmer H2 stimulus tone; record weekly China equity inflow follows
items.summary: The late-July Politburo readout carried stronger-than-expected wording — 'strengthen countercyclical measures with precision and force,' more policy options, and actively expanding domestic demand — after Q2 GDP slowed to 4.3%. Emphasis tilts to faster fiscal execution and tech (AI, quantum, advanced manufacturing). The signal drew a record 3rd-largest weekly China equity inflow (+$21.3bn, BofA/EPFR) and the biggest MLF liquidity injection in five months.
items.actionable: The binary the book was waiting on resolved to the upside and is now being confirmed by flows — the Politburo's forceful language plus a record China inflow support the HK-tech core (Tencent, Xiaomi) and, at the margin, the China-exposed SGX name (CapitaLand China Trust). Watch for follow-through detail at the August policy meetings before adding.

items.headline: SGX REIT season opens strong (Keppel DC REIT DPU +11.3%) as STI banks drag Tuesday
items.summary: Keppel DC REIT posted 1H26 distributable income +18.5% y/y to S$150M and DPU +11.3% to 5.714 cents on positive reversions and acquisitions — a constructive read-through as Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT and CapitaLand China Trust report. But the STI slipped ~0.35% early Tuesday with banks weighing (DBS ~S$73.95, UOB ~S$42.95, OCBC ~S$29.10); MPACT's latest DPU was softer (7.97 cents) and CLCT FY25 DPU fell 14.7% to 4.82 cents on the weaker China/retail sleeve.
items.actionable: A firm datacentre-REIT print is a positive read-through for the S-REIT sleeve into Keppel REIT/Mapletree PACT results, and an easing rate path (oil down, 10Y ~4.62%) would relieve the whole sleeve — but the China-retail drag (CLCT DPU -14.7%) and softening bank guidance temper it. Watch DBS results 6 Aug and the yield backdrop into the FOMC.

items.headline: Big-tech earnings gauntlet this week: MSFT/META (Wed), AAPL/AMZN (Thu) — the AI-capex test
items.summary: Microsoft and Meta report after Wednesday's close and Apple and Amazon after Thursday's, immediately after the FOMC decision. With hyperscaler 2026 capex tracking >$400B, the reports are the key test of whether AI spending is converting to earnings — the crux of the AI-overcapacity debate now driving the semis rout. Nvidia does not report until ~26 Aug.
items.actionable: The mega-cap capex commentary will set the tone for the AI/semis complex — and by read-through the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core — right after the Fed. A reassuring capex-payback readout would stabilize the semis rout; a cautious one would deepen the rotation into Asia's open. Favor Tencent/Xiaomi over pure-semi exposure until this resolves.

items.headline: Malaysia scrutinizes Lynas–Pentagon rare-earth supply deal — political overhang, structural REE positive
items.summary: A Malaysian parliamentary committee is probing Lynas's US$96M US DoD supply agreement (which carries a US$110/kg NdPr price floor) over foreign-policy and strategic-minerals implications — a political overhang for Lynas's Malaysian processing base. The Pentagon offtake nonetheless underpins Western rare-earth economics, favoring producers (MP, Lynas) over development-stage peers.
items.actionable: A headline-risk item for the Lynas leg of the ex-China rare-earth watchlist even as the DoD price floor validates the structural thesis. With China's export controls suspended to 10 Nov (magnet exports at a 6-month high), near-term pricing urgency stays eased — accumulate MP/UUUU on weakness into the control-snap-back catalyst rather than chase.

items.headline: Trump EO bars defense contractors from adversary-sourced critical materials — rare-earth reshoring tailwind
items.summary: Trump signed an executive order (20 Jul) further barring US defense contractors from sourcing critical materials from adversaries and directing the Pentagon to mitigate supply-chain risks. It reinforces the structural US rare-earth reshoring push — the DoD's ~15% MP Materials stake, a $110/kg NdPr price floor and a 10-year magnet offtake, plus ~$1.2bn of OSC loans (Energy Fuels, Phoenix Tailings) in June. Energy Fuels is separately advancing its White Mesa NdPr circuit modifications from July.
items.actionable: Another layer of Western government demand under the ex-China rare-earth watchlist — bullish MP and government-backed UUUU most directly. But with China's controls suspended to 10 Nov, near-term pricing urgency is eased: accumulate on weakness into the control-snap-back catalyst rather than chase the strategic re-rate.
